title: Day-Zero Onprem Orientation + Latency Weirdness (Feb 2027)
content:
Summary:
Day-zero install orientation with customer 'Redford Health' on 2027-02-10. High-level objective: complete initial onprem package install, validate model serving path, hand off runbook. Session uncovered recurring latency spikes for short sequences (p50 ~18ms -> spikes to 120-300ms intermittently). This doc captures the standup notes, immediate mitigations, and action items for follow-up.

Attendees (standup call 09:00 PT):
- Priya Kapoor (install lead)
- Marco Diaz (network eng)
- Aisha Rahman (field SRE)
- Evan Liu (serving-runtime)
- Nora Patel (customer success)
- Customer on-site: Kevin Moore (Infra), Sara Lin (Network)

What happened (observed):
- Installer completed, services healthy per systemd and k8s-lite manifests.
- Model pods reported READY, but application-level latency had repeated 3x-15x spikes for short chat requests (~8-64 tokens).
- Spikes correlated with: a) bursts of small UDP/ICMP ephemeral flows (customer telemetry), b) times when customer NAT gateway replied with IPv6-only route for some external telemetry endpoints.
- During spikes CPU utilization on host was stable, but per-process schedstat showed high involuntary context switches for the runtime process (evan confirmed thread contention).
- Additional symptom: occasional failure to warm KV cache on first request after model reload; subsequent requests fine.

Troubleshooting performed during call:
- Collected tcpdump on mgmt NIC and data NIC; filtered for packets to our internal model-load endpoints. Found packet fragmentation/MTU mismatch on path between node and customer load-balancer (AWS Outpost LB -> customer switch).
- Ran iperf between installer node and customer aggregator: showed asymmetric throughput on small-packet bursts; MTU negotiated 1500 but PMTU discovery suppressed due to ICMP blackhole.
- Captured perf top and perf record: found futex wait queues and kernel preemption events coincident with spikes.
- Verified kernel XPS/GRO settings: customer NICs had GRO enabled plus hardware checksum offload; when combined with TLS offload on the LB it produced re-assembly latency in kernel path.
- Reproduced KV-cache miss pattern by forcing model reloads; enabling large pages changed allocation timing and reduced the first-token latency by ~30%.

Immediate mitigations applied (temporary on-site fixes):
- Marco: disabled GRO and GSO on data NICs (ethtool -K eth1 gro off gso off) — reduced spike amplitude on observed windows.
- Aisha: ramped up tcp_max_syn_backlog and reduced tcp_fin_timeout on nodes to clear ephemeral backlog faster.
- Evan: toggled serving runtime NUMA interleave (set --numa-policy=bind -> prefer) and adjusted thread pool to avoid hot-thread contention for small sequences.
- Priya: updated installer preflight to warn on PMTU/ICMP filtering and added a quick-check step for GRO/GSO. Push queued as github/pr/rr-installer#342.

Root-cause hypotheses (work-in-progress):
1) Network path MTU/ICMP blackholing + NIC offload interaction causing delayed packet delivery for small bursts; kernel reassembly and offload interplay introduces jitter.
2) Runtime thread scheduling + NUMA mapping for small-batch requests creates brief stalls during first-token work (KV cache not hot yet) amplifying observed network jitter.
3) External telemetry flows (UDP) from customer infra coincide with our request bursts, saturating small-packet CPU path leading to increased context switches.

Open blockers / risk items:
- Customer environment prevents ICMP-unreachable messages (IT policy). We need a policy or runbook to surface PMTU issues earlier. Blocker: until policy relaxed, some installs may silently run with degraded latency. (jira/ENG-2041)
- Onprem installer does not currently check for GRO/GSO defaults on combined NIC+LB topologies. We added a preflight warning but full remediation requires a support script and customer approval. (github/pr/rr-installer#342)
- NUMA/default systemd cpuset config on customer images differs from our test images — requires documented defaults and detection in the installer. (jira/ENG-2044)

Action items (owners and ETA):
- Marco: produce a short "network quirks checklist" for field (1 pager) — include PMTU checks, ethtool commands, sample tcpdump filters. ETA 2027-02-15.
- Priya: land and merge rr-installer PR that adds preflight checks and a non-destructive "suggested fixes" mode (PR linked). ETA 2027-02-12 (in review).
- Evan: add runtime flag --numa-warmup to force a cheap synthetic init of KV cache and thread pinning for day-zero installs; create a canary build for field on 2027-02-14. (dev branch: eng-private/numa-warmup)
- Aisha: draft a KB article for SREs describing how to detect ICMP blackhole PMTU issues using curl/trace and ip route get. ETA 2027-02-17.
- Nora: schedule a follow-up customer touchpoint (30 min) after PR merge to validate behavior. ETA 2027-02-16.

Notes to self / informal:
- Need better telemetry to correlate kernel-level context switches with application traces. Consider adding a small eBPF shim to the agent to export involuntary_ctxt_switches per process. Low priority but valuable.
- Consider adding an optional "network sanity" mode to the installer that temporarily disables GRO/GSO for the install window (with explicit customer opt-in). Could be reversible post-install.
- Customer asked for a one-page "what we changed" summary to send to their infra team; Nora to produce.

Meeting minutes (timeline):
- 09:00–09:12: orientation, goals, install status
- 09:12–09:30: observed spike walkthrough, live tcpdump snippets shown
- 09:30–09:50: mitigation trial (disable GRO/GSO, warmup flags), measured p50 p90 improvements
- 09:50–10:00: action item assignment and next check-in scheduling

Measurement snapshots (post-mitigation):
- P50 reduced from 18ms -> 12ms for short requests. P95 reduced from 120ms -> 38ms in 30-minute observation window.
- First-token after model reload latency improved ~30% when largepages enabled; still some variance at p99.

Follow-up check-in: 2027-02-16 09:30 PT (30 min) — verify rr-installer PR merge + re-run iperf + ip route get + new runtime canary.

Attachments / artifacts collected during troubleshooting (reference):
- tcpdump snippet file: /mnt/collection/redford/tcpdump-dayzero-2027-02-10.pcap (uploaded to secure drive)
- iperf logs: /mnt/collection/redford/iperf-burst-2027-02-10.log
- perf flamegraphs: s3://rr-artifacts/redford/perf-flame-20270210.svg

If you are on the field team and find anything new, paste short notes here and ping priya.k@redwood.ai in slack (or slack:#private-deploys).
